title: Mild Mongolian Beef
subtitle: seared strips of beef in a sticky brown sugar, soy and garlic sauce, with onions and jasmine rice: the takeout favourite without the chilies
imageAlt: Glossy dark beef strips with sliced onion over white rice in a white bowl on a navy napkin
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

beforeYouStart.text: Firm the steak in the freezer 20 minutes, then slice across the grain in thin 5 mm strips.

items.name: sirloin steak
items.note: sliced across the grain in 5 mm strips

steps.title: Start the rice
steps.text: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear. Bring it to a boil with the water and a pinch of salt, cover and simmer on low 15 minutes, then rest 10 minutes off the heat with the lid on. Fluff with a fork.

steps.title: Coat
steps.text: Pat the beef dry and toss with the cornstarch until every strip is lightly coated.

steps.title: Sear
steps.text: Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet over high. Sear the beef in 2–3 batches in one layer, 1–2 minutes a side, until browned and crisp at the edges. Move to a plate.

steps.title: Onions
steps.text: Lower the heat to medium-high, add the remaining 1 tbsp oil and the onions and cook 3–4 minutes until just soft. Add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Sauce
steps.text: Add the soy sauce, brown sugar and water and simmer 2–3 minutes until it thickens slightly.

steps.title: Toss
steps.text: Return the beef and toss 1 minute until glossy, coated and at least 63°C (145°F). Serve over the rice.

fixIt.fix: Sear in small batches over high heat; crowding steams it.
Use low-sodium soy, and add a splash of water.
Simmer a minute longer; the cornstarch on the beef thickens it as you toss.

saleTip: Sirloin is the best value for stir-fries; flank is traditional but usually costs more at No Frills.
swap: Flank steak: same method; slice extra thin across the grain.
leftovers: Keeps well for lunches; the coating softens but the flavour is even better.
doneness: Thin strips seared and simmered well past Health Canada's 63°C (145°F) minimum for whole cuts of beef. Reheat to 74°C (165°F).
source: Based on tested Mongolian beef methods (The Woks of Life, Canadian Living): cornstarch-coated beef seared crisp, finished in a brown sugar, soy, garlic and ginger sauce; dried chilies left out.
prepAhead: Slice the beef up to 1 day ahead; coat with cornstarch just before cooking.
reheat: Covered in the microwave 2 minutes, stirring halfway, or in a skillet with a splash of water, until 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: Beef, onion, soy and brown sugar; no fresh ginger.

fancy.note: Steamed broccoli alongside and toasted sesame seeds.

addSteps.title: Broccoli
addSteps.text: Steam or boil the broccoli 3–4 minutes until bright green and tender-crisp. Serve alongside and scatter the sesame seeds over the beef.

plating: Rice to one side, beef piled beside it.

why.0-1: Cornstarch gives the beef a thin crisp crust and thickens the sauce as it's tossed.
why.1-1: Brown sugar makes the sauce sticky and caramel-sweet, balancing the soy.
why.1-5: Onion wedges soften in the sauce and add sweetness.

funFact: Mongolian beef isn't from Mongolia; it was created in Taiwanese and Chinese-American restaurants in the 20th century.
pairs: fried rice instead of plain for a takeout night
